item.title: Disjointness, Orthogonality and Commutativity in $C^*$-Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.31425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize order-theoretic disjointness of two elements $a$ and $b$ in the self-adjoint part of a $C^*$-algebra $A$ via the condition $aAb = \{0\}$ and the trivial intersection of closed two-sided ideals generated by $a$ and $b$. As a consequence, we show that disjoint complements coincide with the self-adjoint parts of annihilator ideals. We also prove that $A$ is commutative whenever every pair of algebraically orthogonal positive contractions in $A$ is disjoint. Finally, we establish corresponding commutativity criteria involving projections for real rank zero $C^*$-algebras.
item.dc:creator: Jani Jokela

item.title: Algebraic derivations and the first \(L^2\)-cohomology of free group factors
item.description: arXiv:2611.32121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(M\) be the von Neumann algebra of a nonabelian free group of finite rank. We prove that its first \(L^2\)-Betti number in the sense of Connes and Shlyakhtenko is infinite. We show that every assignment of values in \(\Aff(M\bar\otimes M^{\op})\) to the standard semicircular generators extends to an algebraic derivation on all of \(M\). The extension follows from a rank identity for the Jacobians of finite systems of polynomial relations. We also prove that, for any \(\mathrm{II}_1\) factor with separable predual, the existence of an outer derivation with these coefficients forces the first \(L^2\)-Betti number to be infinite.
item.dc:creator: J. Huang, K. Kudaybergenov, F. Sukochev, B. Yan

item.title: Monadicity of noncommutative measurable spaces over $C^{\ast}$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.32363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a recent paper, Tobias Fritz and the second author identified $\sigma C^*$-algebras as a tentative noncommutative analogue of measurable spaces. We advance this analogy by establishing monadicity of $\sigma C^*$-algebras over $C^*$-algebras and proving several results of interest to both the category theory and operator algebra communities. In detail, we show that: - The associated probabilistic morphisms, $\sigma$-cpu maps, admit a description via a comonad closely related to the Giry monad. Equivalently, $\sigma$-cpu maps can be characterized by a universal property. - The category of $\sigma C^*$-algebras and $\sigma$-homomorphisms is locally $\aleph_1$-presentable. - $\sigma C^*$-algebras have a tensor product induced by the maximal tensor product of $C^*$-algebras and satisfying an analogous universal property. - The notion of CP-instruments, defined as $\sigma$-additive assignments from a $\sigma$-algebra to a space of completely positive maps, can be adapted to this setting by taking as target the set of $\sigma$-normal completely positive maps between $\sigma C^*$-algebras. This yields a bijective correspondence with $\sigma$-cpu maps out of the tensor product of the previous item.
item.dc:creator: Fosco Loregian, Antonio Lorenzin

item.title: On local embeddability into $C^*(\F_\infty)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.32364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study local embeddability of $C^*$-algebras into $C^*(\F_\infty)$ as an analogue of QWEP in the LLP/WEP picture. We characterize this property by an analog of CP-stability, an approximation property for finite-dimensional operator systems. We show that local embeddability, together with an amenable trace, implies a tracial local lifting property. Combining this observation with the cohomological obstructions of Ioana, Spaas and Wiersma, we prove that the full group $C^*$-algebra $C^*(\SL_3(\Z))$ does not locally embed into $C^*(\F_\infty)$. We obtain the same conclusion for the full $C^*$-algebras of two hyperlinear groups constructed by Thom. To our knowledge, the only previously known obstruction to local embeddability into $C^*(\F_\infty)$ was due to Junge and Pisier.
item.dc:creator: Jean Roydor

item.title: The Universal Frame Characterization of C*-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.32953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a C*-algebra A is a C*-algebra of compact operators if and only if every Hilbert A-module admits a frame. This answers affirmatively the question of Amini, Asadi, Elliott and Khosravi (2017), arising from the problem of Frank and Larson (2002)
item.dc:creator: Mohammad B. Asadi, Zahra Hassanpour-Yakhdani

item.title: An equivariant index theorem for the Heisenberg calculus
item.description: arXiv:2611.31538v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive a local fixed-point formula for the equivariant index of Heisenberg elliptic operators on closed contact manifolds equipped with an action of a compact Lie group preserving the contact form. The formula expresses the character of the equivariant index in terms of a cyclic-cohomological character of the noncommutative Heisenberg principal symbol. The main new ingredient is the construction of traces, one on each fixed-point set, defined by integration over twisted conjugacy classes in the Heisenberg group. The proof proceeds by a K-theoretic reduction to the equivariant index theorem of our paper "Toeplitz operators on contact manifolds and equivariant K-homology".
item.dc:creator: Alexander Gorokhovsky, Erik van Erp

item.title: An extended Matsumoto--Yor property for free GIG distributions
item.description: arXiv:2611.32051v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a two-parameter extension of the Matsumoto--Yor property for free generalized inverse Gaussian distributions. The transformation is the reciprocal form of a known matrix Yang--Baxter map. Our proof combines the independence-preserving property for matrix generalized inverse Gaussian distributions with asymptotic freeness. Since the relevant spectra stay in compact subsets of the positive half-line, continuous functional calculus and polynomial approximation suffice to handle all inverses. The same argument yields the free Matsumoto--Yor property itself for all positive rates of the free Poisson law, including those for which this law has an atom at zero. We also discuss the limit in which one of the two parameters tends to zero: the limiting laws are free Poisson only when the rate is at least one, so for smaller rates this limit does not recover the free Matsumoto--Yor property.
item.dc:creator: Shuhei Nasu, Noriyoshi Sakuma

item.title: Uniformly bounded representations of discrete measured groupoids into finite Von Neumann algebras
item.description: arXiv:2512.21442v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(\mathcal{G},\nu)$ be a $t$-discrete ergodic groupoid. Consider a finite Von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}$ with separable predual. We prove that every uniformly bounded measurable representation $\rho:\mathcal{G} \rightarrow \mathrm{GL}(\mathcal{M})$ into the invertible elements of $\mathcal{M}$ is similar to a unitary representation.
item.dc:creator: Alessio Savini

item.title: Simplicity of q-Gaussian C*-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2606.10723v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that q-Gaussian $C^*$-algebras for $q \in (-1, 1)$ have the Dixmier averaging property, and hence are simple with a unique trace. We argue by combining rapid decay and spectral gap estimates for the commutators with the generators, which are obtained from free probability.
item.dc:creator: Tattwamasi Amrutam, David Jekel, Mateusz Wasilewski

item.title: Nonnuclear Bunce-Deddens algebras
item.description: arXiv:2607.28597v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce nonnuclear Bunce-Deddens algebras, defined as reduced crossed product C*-algebras associated with free odometer actions of nonamenable countable discrete residually finite groups on a Cantor space. These are nonnuclear counterparts to the generalised Bunce-Deddens algebras introduced by Orfanos. For large classes of groups, we show that they share many regularity properties, including real rank zero, stable rank one, strict comparison of positive elements, and admitting a unique tracial state. In many cases, we deduce that they are even selfless and hence pure. Finally, we compute the ordered K-theory and trace pairing of Bunce-Deddens algebras over nonabelian free groups.
item.dc:creator: Jamie Bell

item.title: The relative dimension set of an extremal subfactor of finite index
item.description: arXiv:2611.02336v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Popa's relative dimension set $\Lambda(M,N)$ of an inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors $N\subset M$ consists of the scalars $\alpha$ for which some projection $p\in M$ satisfies $E_N(p)=\alpha1$. Popa computed it for index at most $4$, and for index $d>4$ outside the middle interval $(t_d,1-t_d)$, where $t_d(1-t_d)=d^{-1}$; whether the middle interval meets $\Lambda(M,N)$ for every irreducible inclusion of index $d>4$ has remained open. We show that for every extremal inclusion of finite index $d>4$, the whole interval $[t_d,1-t_d]$ is contained in $\Lambda(M,N)$. Consequently, $\Lambda(M,N)$ depends only on the index for all extremal inclusions of finite index, in particular for all irreducible ones. Extremality cannot be dropped: for $d>4$, Popa's locally trivial inclusions are exactly those whose relative dimension set misses the middle interval. Other non-extremal inclusions can contain the whole middle interval in their relative dimension set, or miss part of it.
item.dc:creator: Julio C\'aceres

item.title: Diagonal and fine tower dimensions for minimal circle homeomorphisms and product actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.19895v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study minimal circle homeomorphisms and their products with Cantor systems, and show that these actions have diagonal dimension at most two and fine tower dimension at least two. Consequently, diagonal dimension, fine tower dimension, and tower dimension are all equal to two for minimal circle homeomorphisms. We also obtain a strict separation between tower dimension and fine tower dimension on a one-dimensional space.
item.dc:creator: Kang Li, Geng Wang

item.title: Quasi-locality and weak containment for Roe algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.21255v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish two characterisations of Property A for discrete metric spaces of bounded geometry in terms of the Roe algebra. More precisely, we show that such a space has Property A if and only if its Roe algebra coincides with its quasi-local algebra, also equivalent to the canonical quotient map from the maximal Roe algebra to the reduced one being injective. We also prove, without assuming Property A, that the strongly quasi-local algebra always coincides with the Roe algebra. As applications, we show that a discrete group is exact whenever its full group $C^*$-algebra has the local lifting property. We also show that the maximal injective crossed-product functor agrees with the reduced one precisely for exact discrete groups.
item.dc:creator: Benyin Fu, Kang Li, Jiawen Zhang

item.title: An isolated complex Hadamard matrix with nonzero defect
item.description: arXiv:2611.20136v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The defect of a complex Hadamard matrix is the real dimension of the solution space obtained by linearizing the row orthogonality equations in the phases of the entries, with the first row and column fixed. It is known that defect zero implies isolation up to Hadamard equivalence. The converse, whether every isolated complex Hadamard matrix has defect zero, was open and is the square-matrix case of a conjecture of Banica, Ozteke and Pittau. We answer this question in the negative. We exhibit a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of order 13 with entries among the sixth roots of unity and show that it is isolated and has defect one. We prove isolation by showing that no nonzero solution of the linearized equations satisfies the second order condition obtained by the second author for directions of convergence of sequences of Hadamard matrices. In the language of commuting squares of matrix algebras, the example shows that an isolated commuting square can fail the span condition introduced by the second author as a sufficient condition for isolation.
item.dc:creator: Shannon Hall, Remus Nicoara

item.title: The standard filtration of Leavitt path algebras and topological full groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.28188v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider several problems related to the growth of Leavitt path algebras with respect to the natural length filtration. We define the generating function of the series of dimensions of the successive quotients of this filtration and show that it is a rational function with poles which are reciprocal of the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix, a fact which is related to recent results by Bock, Gil Canto, Mart\'in Barquero, Mart\'in Gonz\'alez, Ruiz Campos and Sebandal on algebraic entropy of Leavitt path algebras. We also consider the filtration induced in the topological full group of the Renault-Deaconu groupoid of the defining graph and study the growth of the associated series. In the particular case of Thompson's group $V$, we find double exponential upper and lower bounds for this growth. We also prove related results for the group $F$ and for some submonoids.
item.dc:creator: Conchita Mart\'inez-P\'erez, Sof\'ia Sir\'on
